attacks.claim: Retrieval (chunks and embeddings derived from customer documents) moves to a Vector Store provisioned only in us-east-2, with no EU region yet. Week 2 re-embeds ~41M chunks into it and dual-writes new documents, and week 4 cuts all tenants over. This violates the agreed constraint that customer documents and derived data stay in the EU, and generation in eu-west-1 does not cure it.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." / "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: The 4,100-case regression suite is the agreed release gate for any model change, but the plan runs it in week 6+, after cutover in week 4. Atlas-L and the new per-practice prompts reach all tenants without passing the gate.
attacks.evidence: "so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: Week 3 irreversibly releases the A100 reservation and deletes the fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters. This happens before cutover (week 4) and before any regression result exists, and the plan keeps no export or copy. If Nimbus quality, latency or residency fails, the self-hosted model cannot be restored or reproduced.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation (saves $18.4k/mo from the next billing cycle) and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: Quality parity is asserted from 25 support-inbox questions judged by two lawyers, which is too small to support a release decision. The core assumption that per-practice LoRA behaviour can be reproduced by system prompts is unprototyped and untested.
attacks.evidence: "This confirms quality parity or better" / "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is evidenced only for the generation path. Retention, DPA coverage and EU processing for embed-3 and Vector Store (which hold chunks and embeddings) are unstated, and there is no tenant data deletion on churn or DPA termination and no audit evidence.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." / ABSENT: retention, DPA coverage, deletion and audit for embed-3 and Vector Store

attacks.claim: The latency evidence does not support the comparison. It is p95 time-to-first-token only, from one week of 1,000 requests, measured from Frankfurt against Dublin generation alone, excluding the us-east-2 retrieval hop. End-to-end latency, the 200k-context cases and the OOM-prone long-context loads that motivated the migration are unmeasured, and the vLLM 910 ms figure has no stated profile.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05), vs 910 ms on vLLM."

attacks.claim: Rate-limit headroom is 3x on average, but the plan gives no burst analysis, backoff or queuing, and no per-tenant fairness. The week-2 re-embed and dual-writes run against the same 120 req/s quota as live traffic, so they can starve production.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus rate limits: our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: No failure-mode design exists for the new external dependency across generation, embeddings and retrieval. There are no timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, fallback path or alerting, and no SLA is discussed, even though the migration is meant to reduce on-call load.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: timeout/retry/fallback/circuit-breaker/alerting design; Section 7 lists only rate limits and latency.

attacks.claim: Single-vendor lock-in with no reversal path. Week 5 deletes pgvector, the vLLM manifests and the GPU node pool, all before retrieval and generation are validated against the regression gate. Rolling back after week 5 would require rebuilding the index and redeploying inference.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: The dual-write and backfill procedure is underspecified. The plan does not say how writes stay consistent between pgvector and Vector Store during the window, how tenants are ordered for migration, or how the 41M-chunk re-embed is verified against source documents.
attacks.evidence: "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: The cost savings rest on an unsupported $7,900 generation estimate with no token volume or pricing basis. Dual-running in weeks 2 to 5, re-embedding cost, and the cost of longer 200k-context prompts are not budgeted.

Per-tenant isolation depends on tenant-scoped keys in a preview service, with no cross-tenant isolation test or audit. The rotation mechanism for tenant-scoped keys under the 30-day policy is not described.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key" / "rotated every 30 days"

attacks.claim: Retrieval is bundled into the generation migration to drop pgvector, which couples two decisions. A retrieval rollback would then force a generation rollback, and the preview dependency is taken on for storage convenience.
attacks.evidence: "Moving retrieval in the same project lets us drop pgvector and its index-maintenance jobs."

attacks.claim: Success is not defined from the lawyers' side. The plan names cost, OOMs and context length but no user-facing quality or latency targets.
